task_summary: Plan concise release notes for Atlas Notes 2.4.1. The required outcome states that the maintenance update fixes a sync status label that could retain stale text after reconnecting, adds no user-facing feature, and does not change the existing queuing of offline edits. Remove any claim of faster sync. Keep editorial polish optional and verify the final note against the four required facts with no extra promise.

decision_record.decision: Use a separate outcome contract and narrative plan.
decision_record.because: The contract preserves required facts; the narrative may explain rationale and sequencing without creating requirements.
decision_record.risk: Narrative wording could be mistaken for an additional product promise.

decision_record.decision: Remove all language implying faster sync performance.
decision_record.because: Performance is outside update 2.4.1 and would create an unsupported customer-visible promise.
decision_record.risk: Residual phrases such as “improved sync” could still imply a performance gain.

decision_record.decision: State that offline edits were already queued before this update.
decision_record.because: The current draft omits this required continuity fact and could imply the update introduced offline queuing.
decision_record.risk: Loose wording could falsely present existing behavior as new.

decision_record.decision: Keep editorial improvements optional and subordinate to factual review.
decision_record.because: Tone and brevity may improve readability but must not alter release scope or acceptance criteria.
decision_record.risk: Editorial expansion could introduce feature, reliability, or performance claims.

proposed_change_manifest.change: Require the note to identify Atlas Notes 2.4.1, describe the stale sync-status-label fix after reconnecting, state that no user-facing feature was added, and clarify that offline edits were already queued.
proposed_change_manifest.reason: These are the four facts the reviewer must confirm.

proposed_change_manifest.change: Delete or rewrite any wording that says or implies sync is faster, quicker, or performance-enhanced.
proposed_change_manifest.reason: Sync performance is not part of this maintenance update.

proposed_change_manifest.change: Present the release context first, the reconnect label fix second, and the continuity and no-new-feature facts next. Add no requirements beyond the outcome contract.
proposed_change_manifest.reason: This sequence keeps the note concise while making the correction and scope boundary clear.

proposed_change_manifest.change: Permit concise wording, sentence-flow, and tone improvements only when they preserve the required facts and add no customer promise.
proposed_change_manifest.reason: Editorial polish is useful but is not part of the release outcome.

proposed_change_manifest.change: Have a reviewer confirm the four required facts are present and that no extra promise appears.
proposed_change_manifest.reason: This is the specified acceptance check and guards against semantic and scope drift.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A1 The release covers version 2.4.1 of Atlas Notes.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The outcome contract requires the note to identify Atlas Notes 2.4.1.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A2 The update fixes a sync status label that could show stale text after reconnecting.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The planned required facts include the stale sync-status-label fix after reconnecting.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A3 The update adds no new user-facing feature.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The outcome contract explicitly requires stating that no user-facing feature was added.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A4 The note must mention that offline edits were already queued before this update.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The plan requires wording that offline edits were already queued, preventing the behavior from appearing new.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A5 The note must avoid promising faster sync performance.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The promise boundary removes faster-sync claims and related performance implications.

acceptance_mapping.atom: A6 The acceptance check is a reviewer confirming the four required facts and no extra promise.
acceptance_mapping.evidence: The acceptance review assigns a reviewer to confirm all four facts and the absence of extra promises.
